summary: First compare against the routed netlist (the reference the #109 analysis named as the remaining hypothesis: 'an LVS run against a reference that is the netlist the layout implements'). Verdict: mismatch, exit 3 - the grade is unchanged and the residue barely moved: nets matched 408 (r12, against design/netlist/slice_asap7.v: 352), net.split 15269 (r12 15331), net.merged 14967 (r12 15246), device.unmatched 55444 (r12 56195), hints.rejected 67. That refutes the different-netlist hypothesis: the layout was placed and routed from this exact netlist, so a correct extraction of the stream must match it, and it does not. Reference totals differ from r12's because layout/slice_routed.v is the post-route netlist: 15501 nets / 28862 devices (r12's synthesis reference: 15718 / 29356).
request_notes: The r12 request verbatim apart from the reference netlist path (../../layout/slice_routed.v) and the scratch pdk_root / pin_order_files paths: pinned lambdapdk v0.2.17 tree (archive sha256 ac7e950c4d0394a829658b6e219fea4a4b0c61a998183d5520f8b9e38c6efff2), re-fetched into /tmp scratch, not committed. options carry only flatten_layout and finfet_bulk; supply_nets is the default six-net list.

previous.note: r12 ran the same stream against design/netlist/slice_asap7.v (the synthesis output); r13 runs it against layout/slice_routed.v (the routed output of the same flow) and the mismatch is unchanged, so the reference netlist choice is not the cause.

tracing.what: With the different-netlist hypothesis refuted, the residue was traced on the committed stream (predictive-model tool results only; analysis of committed files plus one klt extract run and throwaway-uvx klayout Python measurements). Cell-internal extraction is correct: the r9 single-cell probe still stands, a new two-instance abutment probe (two R0 BUFx4_ASAP7_75t_R at exact abutment, one local klt lvs run under the same pinned klt) leaves the cells' internal AN nets separate, and klt extract on the routed stream reproduces every library cell's CDL topology hierarchically.
tracing.extract: uvx --with klayout --from klayout-tools==0.9.1 klt extract layout/slice_routed.gds --deck asap7 --top slice (one local run, exit 0, netlist in scratch, not evidence): top circuit has 2594 X instances and 2955 nets; 855 of its nets carry exactly one cell pin against 6 such nets in layout/slice_routed.v (1649 reference nets carry exactly two, a clean driver-load chain); rx_clk reaches 179 cell pins against 528 in layout/slice_routed.v. The extract also warns that three layers (3/251 88 shapes, 100/0 92, 235/5 1) are outside the deck's connectivity graph.
tracing.geometry: Merging the M2-M6 routing layers of the committed stream with the klayout Python module, joining layers only through via cuts (flood fill absorbing each via layer then the next metal until fixpoint), yields 215 components; the largest spans the whole die (bbox (0,4696)-(95340,176744) dbu) and holds 99.3 percent of the stack's routing area (4707.3e6 of 4739.8e6 dbu^2). Merged M2 alone keeps 14361 disjoint shapes and merged M3 7850, so the joins are through via cuts, not same-layer overlap. At M1 level the union of M1/V0/LIG/LISD keeps 9415 webs, the magnitude the cell-pin population implies. Sub-minimum-width M2 shapes exist on the committed stream: 87048 x 72 dbu (21.762 x 0.018 um) shapes on 20/0 both inside the core and outside it (y 4284 dbu against a core starting at 7872; y 178164 against a core ending at 172320).
tracing.conclusion: The committed stream's M2-M6 wiring is one electrically connected web: power straps and signal routing are shorted together on the upper layers. No LVS reference can match a stream in that state, which is the determined cause of the r5-r13 net.split/net.merged residue. The defect is in the routed stream, not in the reference or the compare options. Whether the short is created by klt place-and-route's DEF or by its DEF->GDS merge is not determined here (the DEF is a scratch artifact of regen.py and was not kept); layout/pnr/regen.py re-runs the flow and can separate the two.
